proof.text: (i_X is a surjective closed immersion and a homeomorphism.) By the definition of the reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is the closed subscheme of $X$ cut out by the nilradical $\mathcal N_X$, $i_X$ is its canonical closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $i_X$ is the identity on underlying sets: the support of $\mathcal O_X/\mathcal N_X$ is all of $X$, since on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ we have $V(\mathrm{nil}(R))=\operatorname{Spec}R$ (every prime contains every nilpotent). Hence $i_X$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. A closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its (closed) image, here all of $X$, so $i_X$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces. (Mathlib: $i_X$ is `X.nilradical.subschemeι`, a closed immersion by the instance at Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean:94; surjectivity is `range_subschemeι` (IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:493) with `Scheme.support_nilradical : X.nilradical.support = ⊤` (IdealSheaf/Basic.lean:533).)

proof.text: ($X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced.) Let $x\in X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and let $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ be an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum] containing $i_X(x)$. By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] the sections of $\mathcal N_X$ over $U$ form the nilradical $\mathrm{nil}(R)$, so the open subscheme $i_X^{-1}(U)$ of $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathrm{nil}(R))$ (the closed subscheme of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ cut out by the quasi-coherent ideal $\widetilde{\mathrm{nil}(R)}$, as in the proof of Stacks 01J3: $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$). The ring $R/\mathrm{nil}(R)$ is reduced: if $\bar f^n=0$ then $f^n\in\mathrm{nil}(R)$, so $f^{nm}=0$ for some $m$, so $f\in\mathrm{nil}(R)$ and $\bar f=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathrm{nil}(R))$ is reduced [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], so the local ring $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathrm{red}},x}$, which is the local ring of the open subscheme $i_X^{-1}(U)$ at $x$, is reduced. As $x$ was arbitrary, $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. (Mathlib route: `subschemeCover` (IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:507) covers $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ by `Spec (Γ(X, U) ⧸ X.nilradical.ideal U)`, where `X.nilradical.ideal U = (⊥ : Ideal _).radical` by `radical_ideal`; `Ideal.isRadical_iff_quotient_reduced`, `affine_isReduced_iff` and `IsReduced.of_openCover` (Properties.lean:133) conclude. The source repository proves exactly this pattern for `vanishingIdeal Z` in `Scheme.IdealSheafData.isReduced_subscheme_vanishingIdeal`, and Mathlib's `vanishingIdeal_top : vanishingIdeal ⊤ = X.nilradical` (IdealSheaf/Basic.lean:646) specializes it to $Z=X$.)

proof.text: ($i_X$ is a universal homeomorphism.) Let $g:X'\to X$ be a morphism of schemes and $p:X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_XX'\to X'$ the projection from the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Since $i_X$ is a closed immersion (step 1), $p$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; since $i_X$ is surjective (step 1), $p$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $p$ is a homeomorphism of $|X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_XX'|$ onto the closed subset $p(|X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_XX'|)$ of $X'$, and this subset is all of $X'$ because $p$ is surjective. So $p$ is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces (an embedding that is surjective is a homeomorphism; Mathlib `isHomeomorph_iff_isEmbedding_surjective`, Topology/Homeomorph/Lemmas.lean:520). As $g$ was arbitrary, $i_X$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].

title: The reduction of a scheme is reduced and a universal homeomorphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $i_X:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ its reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Then $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and $i_X$ is a surjective closed immersion and a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]: for every morphism of schemes $X'\to X$ the base change $X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_XX'\to X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces.
